From d814567942ff6ac73869052bdb8ca911364e5eb0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Steven Rostedt (VMware)" <rostedt@goodmis.org>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2021 12:49:58 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] mm, tracing: Fix kmem_cache_free trace event to not print
 stale pointers

The update to kmem_cache_free trace event added printing of the slab name in
the trace event. But it only stores the pointer of the name which will be
printed as a string when the event is read some time in the future. This is
dangerous because the name could be freed in the mean time and when reading
the trace event it would try to dereference the string name by the pointer
to the name that has been freed.

Instead, use the trace event helper macros __string(), __assign_str(), and
__get_str() that are for this very case.

Cc: Jacob Wen <jian.w.wen@oracle.com>
Fixes: 3544de8ee6e4 ("mm, tracing: record slab name for kmem_cache_free()")
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (VMware) <rostedt@goodmis.org>

diff --git a/include/trace/events/kmem.h b/include/trace/events/kmem.h
index 40845b0d5dad..3a60b6b6db32 100644
--- a/include/trace/events/kmem.h
+++ b/include/trace/events/kmem.h
@@ -144,17 +144,17 @@ TRACE_EVENT(kmem_cache_free,
 	TP_STRUCT__entry(
 		__field(	unsigned long,	call_site	)
 		__field(	const void *,	ptr		)
-		__field(	const char *,	name		)
+		__string(	name,	name	)
 	),
 
 	TP_fast_assign(
 		__entry->call_site	= call_site;
 		__entry->ptr		= ptr;
-		__entry->name		= name;
+		__assign_str(name, name);
 	),
 
 	TP_printk("call_site=%pS ptr=%p name=%s",
-		  (void *)__entry->call_site, __entry->ptr, __entry->name)
+		  (void *)__entry->call_site, __entry->ptr, __get_str(name))
 );
 
 TRACE_EVENT(mm_page_free,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `include/trace/events/kmem.h`**
   - The `TRACE_EVENT(kmem_cache_free)` structure has been modified:
     - The field type for `name` has been changed from `const char *` to `__string(name, name)`, which is a macro that handles string storage safely.
     - In the `TP_fast_assign` section, the assignment of `name` has been updated from `__entry->name = name;` to `__assign_str(name, name);`, ensuring that the string is properly assigned using the new macro.
     - In the `TP_printk` section, the way the name is printed has been changed from `__entry->name` to `__get_str(name)`, which retrieves the string safely.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `include/trace/events/kmem.h` are interconnected as they collectively address a bug related to the handling of string pointers in the `kmem_cache_free` trace event. The change from a raw pointer to a managed string representation prevents potential dereferencing of freed memory, thus enhancing the safety and reliability of the trace event. Each modification builds upon the previous one, ensuring that the string is stored, assigned, and retrieved correctly without risking stale pointer dereferencing.

Here is the commit message:
mm, tracing: Fix kmem_cache_free trace event to not print
 stale pointers

The update to kmem_cache_free trace event added printing of the slab name in
the trace event. But it only stores the pointer of the name which will be
printed as a string when the event is read some time in the future. This is
dangerous because the name could be freed in the mean time and when reading
the trace event it would try to dereference the string name by the pointer
to the name that has been freed.

Instead, use the trace event helper macros __string(), __assign_str(), and
__get_str() that are for this very case.

Cc: Jacob Wen <jian.w.wen@oracle.com>
Fixes: 3544de8ee6e4 ("mm, tracing: record slab name for kmem_cache_free()")
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (VMware) <rostedt@goodmis.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the use of a pointer to the slab name in the `kmem_cache_free` trace event, which can lead to dereferencing a freed pointer when the trace event is read at a later time. This occurs because the slab name may be deallocated before the trace event is accessed, resulting in a stale pointer and potential memory access violations.

```c
__entry->name		= name;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `kmem_cache_free` trace event stores a pointer to the slab name, which can be deallocated before the trace event is accessed. This results in a stale pointer that leads to dereferencing a freed memory location when the trace event is read, causing potential memory access violations.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
__string(	name, name	)
__assign_str(name, name);
```
Reason:
The fix replaces the direct pointer storage with the use of trace event helper macros `__string()` and `__assign_str()`, which safely manage the string data. This ensures that the slab name is copied and stored correctly, preventing the issue of dereferencing a stale pointer when the trace event is accessed later.
